card.name: Words leading into risk comparisons
card.fires_on: Small words like "a", "risk" or "drug" that come right before a described adverse effect or risk difference, such as a reduction, higher rate, or drug-induced harm. Seen in warning text about side effects.

modes.label: Article before an effect
modes.description: The word "a" just before a described effect such as reduction or higher rate.
modes.example: Corticosteroids, including mometasone furoate monohydrate nasal spray, may cause<< a>> reduction in growth velocity when administered to pediatric

modes.label: Risk before differences
modes.description: The word "risk" opening a phrase about drug versus placebo differences.
modes.example: with the highest incidence in MDD. The<< risk>> differences (drug vs placebo), however,

modes.label: Drug before induced
modes.description: The word "drug" just before a hyphenated harm term.
modes.example: There has been no evidence of<< drug>>-induced hepatotoxicity in the piog

card.writes: It nudges the next word toward ones like "associated" or "safe", which fits phrases about what is linked to a drug.
card.plain: It fires on a small word just before a side effect or risk is spelled out in a warning.
